units.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for Python is a Python library for working with 3D documents, supporting import and export of formats including .obj, .stl, .gltf, .glb, .dae, .3mf, and .fbx. It enables developers to create, manipulate, and inspect 3D scenes using classes such as aspose.threed.Scene, aspose.threed.Node, aspose.threed.Mesh, and aspose.threed.A3DObject. The library is suitable for Python developers building applications that process 3D geometry, metadata, and materials without requiring a full commercial suite. It requires Python 3.7 or higher and is distributed under the MIT license.
Aspose.3D FOSS for Python reads .obj, .stl, .gltf, .glb, .dae, and .3mf files using Scene.open(), which auto-detects the format from the file extension or an explicit FileFormat instance.
Aspose.3D FOSS for Python writes scenes to .obj, .stl, .gltf, .glb, and .3mf files using Scene.save() with format-specific save options provided by FileFormat.create_save_options().

Aspose.3D FOSS for Python builds and traverses a scene graph using Node.create_child_node(), Node.add_entity(), and Node.child_nodes, where each node carries an independent Transform with translation, rotation, and scaling properties.

Aspose.3D FOSS for Python authoring and editing mesh data directly through Mesh.control_points, Mesh.create_polygon(), and Mesh.to_mesh() from primitives, as demonstrated in examples for building custom geometry and exporting to .stl and .gltf.

Aspose.3D FOSS for Python assigns LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, or PbrMaterial to nodes, setting diffuse, metallic, and roughness properties directly, as shown in examples that export scenes with shaded primitives to .gltf and .stl.
Aspose.3D FOSS for Python constructs keyframe animations using AnimationClip, AnimationNode, and KeyframeSequence, and stores skeletal bind-pose data with Pose.
Aspose.3D FOSS for Python triangulates arbitrary polygon data into triangle fans using PolygonModifier.triangulate() and builds polygon geometry with PolygonBuilder.
Aspose.3D FOSS for Python constructs parameterized primitives such as Box, Sphere, and Cylinder, and converts them to editable Mesh geometry by calling their to_mesh() method.
Create a box primitive, assign a Lambert material, and export the scene to glTF.
The following examples demonstrate common workflows: creating primitives with materials, building meshes from control points, exporting to various formats, and inspecting mesh geometry.
Create a sphere with a PBR material and save it as STL.
Build a mesh, assign a PBR material, and export to glTF JSON.
Build a triangle mesh and export it to ASCII STL.
Convert a Box primitive to a mesh and count control points.
Build a cube mesh and export it to uncompressed 3MF.

The primary entry point is the aspose.threed.Scene class, which loads and saves scene graphs built from aspose.threed.Node objects, each containing a Transform, an optional Mesh-derived Entity, and zero or more Material instances. The aspose.threed.FileFormat class provides format-specific import and export capabilities.

The aspose.threed.Scene class provides Scene.open() and Scene.save() methods to load and write scene graphs, and exposes Scene.root_node, Scene.animation_clips, Scene.poses, Scene.library, Scene.sub_scenes, Scene.current_animation_clip, Scene.asset_info, Scene.clear, and Scene.create_animation_clip to inspect and manipulate the scene graph.

The aspose.threed.Node class represents nodes in the scene graph, each holding a Transform, an optional Mesh-derived Entity, and zero or more Material instances, with methods such as Node.add_child_node, Node.add_entity, Node.get_child, Node.select_objects, Node.evaluate_global_transform, Node.get_bounding_box, Node.global_transform, Node.transform, Node.material, Node.materials, Node.child_nodes, Node.entities, Node.entity, Node.parent_node, Node.meta_datas, Node.excluded, Node.visible, Node.create_child_node, and Node.merge.

The aspose.threed.Mesh class and aspose.threed.PolygonBuilder class support mesh construction and modification, with aspose.threed.entities.PolygonModifier providing static methods such as triangulate to convert polygonal geometry.

The aspose.threed.shading module provides material classes including aspose.threed.shading.LambertMaterial, aspose.threed.shading.PhongMaterial, and aspose.threed.shading.PbrMaterial for defining surface appearance.
The aspose.threed.AnimationClip class, along with aspose.threed.AnimationNode, aspose.threed.KeyframeSequence, and aspose.threed.Pose, supports animation definition and playback in the scene graph.
The aspose.threed.entities module provides primitive shape classes such as aspose.threed.Box, aspose.threed.Sphere, and aspose.threed.Cylinder for procedural geometry generation.
The aspose.threed.formats module supports input formats including .obj, .stl, .gltf, .glb, .dae, and .3mf, with format-specific load and save options provided by the aspose.threed.FileFormat class.
The aspose.threed.utilities module provides common data types such as aspose.threed.utilities.Vector3 and aspose.threed.utilities.Vector4 for geometric calculations.
The A3DObject class represents a base object in the scene hierarchy that supports named properties and can be queried for property values.
The AnimationChannel class represents a single animated property channel that stores keyframe sequences and default values.
The AnimationClip class represents a container for animation data that defines a time range and contains animation nodes.
The AnimationNode class represents a node in an animation hierarchy that can hold bind points and sub-animations.
The AssetInfo class holds metadata about a 3D asset such as author, creation time, coordinate system, and unit scale factor.
The BindPoint class represents a binding location that connects animation channels to scene properties.
The BonePose class represents the transformation state of a bone in either local or world space.
The Box class represents a box primitive with configurable dimensions and segmentation.
The Camera class represents a camera entity that defines a view frustum for rendering.
The Circle class represents a circular primitive defined by radius and segmentation.
The Curve class represents a parametric curve entity in three-dimensional space.
The CustomObject class represents a user-defined object that extends the base A3DObject functionality.
The Cylinder class represents a cylindrical primitive with configurable height and segmentation.
The Dish class represents a dish-shaped primitive with configurable radii and segmentation.
The Ellipse class represents an elliptical primitive defined by radii and segmentation.
The Entity class represents a renderable or manipulable object in a scene that can be assigned to nodes.
The Extrapolation class defines how animation values are computed beyond the defined keyframe range.
The ExtrapolationType class enumerates supported methods for extrapolating animation values.
The FileFormat class provides utilities for identifying and working with supported 3D file formats.
The Frustum class represents a truncated pyramid primitive used for defining camera view volumes.
The Geometry class represents a geometric entity that can be converted to mesh data for rendering.
The GlobalTransform class represents a complete transformation matrix applied to an object in world space.
The INamedObject interface defines a contract for objects that can be assigned a name.
The ImageRenderOptions class holds settings that control how a scene is rendered to an image.
The Interpolation class enumerates supported methods for interpolating between keyframes.
The KeyFrame class represents a single keyframe with a time value and associated data.
The KeyframeSequence class represents a sequence of keyframes used to define animated values over time.
The Light class represents a light source entity that inherits camera properties for rendering illumination.
The LinearExtrusion class represents a 3D shape created by extruding a 2D profile along a straight path.
The Mesh class represents a polygonal mesh geometry composed of vertices and polygons.
The Node class represents a transformable container in the scene hierarchy that can hold entities.
The Plane class represents an infinite planar primitive used for geometric operations.
The PolygonBuilder class provides utilities for constructing polygonal meshes programmatically.
The Pose class represents a static transformation pose that can be applied to scene objects.
The PoseType class enumerates the types of poses supported in the animation system.
The Primitive class represents a basic geometric shape that can be used to construct more complex models.
The Property class represents a single named property with a value and type information.
The PropertyCollection class represents a collection of named properties associated with an object.
The Scene class represents a complete 3D scene containing nodes, entities, and animation data.
The SceneObject class represents an object that belongs to a scene and can participate in the scene hierarchy.
The Sphere class represents a sphere primitive in Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.
The StepMode class defines enumeration values for step mode settings in Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.
The Transform class encapsulates geometric transformations such as translation, rotation, and scaling for 3D objects in Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.
The WeightedMode class defines enumeration values for weighted mode settings in Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.
The Bone class represents a bone used in skeletal animation within Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.
The BoneLinkMode class defines enumeration values for bone linking behavior in Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.
The Deformer class serves as the base class for mesh deformation operations in Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.

The InvalidOperationException class is raised when an invalid operation is performed during polygon building in Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.
The PolygonModifier class provides utilities for modifying polygonal meshes in Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.
The ReferenceMode class defines enumeration values for reference modes in Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.
The TextureMapping class defines enumeration values for texture mapping strategies in Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.

The how-to guides and FAQ provide task-focused answers for common 3D-processing questions.

Aspose.3D FOSS for Python provides read and write support for OBJ, STL, glTF, and COLLADA, plus basic scene inspection and node manipulation, targeting Python 3.7 through 3.12.

No file format registers an importer or exporter for PDF, PLY, RVM, U3D, JT, AMF, HTML5, A3DW, USD, or Draco in this build — PdfSaveOptions, PlyLoadOptions, DracoSaveOptions, and similar option classes exist as public types, but Scene.open() and Scene.save() cannot detect or dispatch any of these extensions, and raise a RuntimeError if you try.

FBX support is experimental: FbxImporter has a working tokenizer and parser but no bundled test opens a real .fbx fixture through it, and FbxExporter.save() and save_to_stream() both raise NotImplementedError outright, so FBX is import-only at best.

COLLADA import works, but COLLADA export is not reachable through Scene.save() because IOService's exporter lookup reaches FbxExporter before ColladaExporter, so the lookup fails before a working ColladaExporter is ever consulted.

Import load and save options classes from their format-specific submodules (aspose.threed.formats.obj, aspose.threed.formats.stl, aspose.threed.formats.gltf, aspose.threed.formats.collada), not from the shared top-level aspose.threed.formats package, because the top-level package resolves to a broken duplicate for OBJ, STL, glTF, and COLLADA.

Scene.render() and the entire aspose.threed.render module (Renderer, RenderFactory, Viewport, and related classes) raise NotImplementedError, and Texture and TextureBase raise NotImplementedError on construction, so image-backed textures cannot be created.

Boolean/CSG mesh operations, NURBS sampling, point cloud generation, axis system handling, and watermark encoding/decoding all raise NotImplementedError, and TransformBuilder methods are unavailable; use Transform's translation, rotation, and scaling properties instead.

Install the package in editable mode and run the test suite using the unittest module against the tests directory. The suite covers 34 test files under tests/. Releases run through the publish workflow.
This package is the open-source variant; the commercial product adds additional file format support, advanced rendering capabilities, and enterprise-grade support options.
